High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This is the first application under Section 389(1) of CrPC seeking for suspension of sentence and bail filed on behalf of accused/appellant - Ramu Singh, who has been convicted under Section 3 read with Section 4 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo seven years' rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/-, five years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,500/- under Section 450 of IPC and two years' rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.500/- under Section 506 Part II of IPC with default stipulation vide impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 30.10.2017 passed by the Sessions Judge, Bhind in Sessions Trial No. 100 of 2015.

In a nutshell, the prosecution case is that prosecutrix, aged around 17 years (PW2), lodged a report at Police Station Dehat, District Bhind on 01-01- 2015 alleging therein that her father is posted as ASI (CRPF) at Raipur and on the date of incident i.e. 01-01-2015, her brother (PW4) was in Gwalior and her mother had gone to her brother at Gwalior for five-six days.
Her elder sister (PW3) had gone to market at around 12:00 in the noon, she was alone at home.
A friend of her brother - Ramu Bhadoriya (appellant- accused) came to her house and in absence of family members, accused asked her to give him water.
When she went inside the room to get water, accused followed her inside and dragged her inside the room.
When she screamed, accused pressed her mouth and threatened if she screams, he would strangle her to death.
Accused threw her on bed and forcibly committed rape with her.
She kept crying.
Meanwhile, her sister arrived, seeing whom accused ran away from her house.
Prosecutrix narrated the incident to her elder sister.
Her elder sister also informed her brother on phone.
After her brother and mother returned home, she told them about the incident and thereafter, along with her brother, she went to Police Station to lodge the report.
On the basis of which, PS Dehat, District Bhind registered FIR for offence punishable under Sections 376, 506 of IPC was registered against appellant.
Appellant was arrested.
Prosecutrix was sent for medical examination.
Relevant seizures were made.
Statements of witnesses were recorded.
After completion of investigation and other formalities, challan was filed before Court of JMFC from where the case was committed to the Sessions Court for its trial.

sentences.text: trial Court convicted and sentenced present appellant for offence, as narrated above.
It is contended on behalf of appellant that appellant has been falsely implicated.
No documents regarding determination of age of prosecutrix was either produced by her parents or by prosecution before the Court.
Although Dr. Anshu Mishra (PW6) had referred for X-ray examination of the prosecutrix but no X-ray report was produced for determination of age.

As per the medical report,
no external or internal injury was found on the body of prosecutrix, therefore, no offence of rape is made out against appellant.
The trial Court has committed an error in convicting and sentencing the present appellant.
Appellant was on bail during trial and he did not misuse the liberty so granted to him.
The fine amount has already been deposited by appellant.
Appeal is of year 2017 and its final outcome will take some time.
Appellant is ready to abide by all the terms and conditions that may be imposed by this Court while considering his application.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of suspension of sentence and bail.
State counsel has vehemently opposed the contentions stating that there is sufficient material available on record against the present appellant.
There is no infirmity in passing the impugned judgment as there is active participation of the present appellant in commission of offence.
On these grounds, he has prayed for dismissal of the application.
Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the evidence against the present appellant, no case of grant of bail is made out.
Accordingly, I.A.No.2489 of 2020 is hereby rejected.
(RAVI MALIMATH) (MILIND RAMES  CHIEF JUSTICE JUDG  Ch Ramu Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151820026/
